title: Husk O'Hare's Wolverines under his direction; Des Moines
summary: Dick Voynow becomes an A and R man and gives him the Wolverines name; he books the Austin High men through Husk O'Hare, playing Des Moines.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs

blocks.x: We did that vaudeville for a little bit. I had gotten the Austin Highschool Gang then. By that time I had Davey Tough, I had Dick Voynow get Davey Tough on drums, my brother on guitar and banjo. My brother-in-law, Jim Lanigan on string bass and Bud Freeman on tenor saxophone and Teschemaker on clarinet and we had Floyd O'Brien on trombone. And we were doing this vaudeville.

So Dick Voynow got an offer to go with Brunswick records to be an A and R man there and to record different bands. So he says well, I tell you what we'll do kid, he says you can have the name the Wolverines and book the band. So what happened was we, I just got my, that was the band. Let me see, oh yes, there was Dave North at piano. On piano and then I mentioned the rest of the guys there.
I booked the band through Husk O'Hare. We were booked out...
Oh, that accounts for my seeing in print somewhere
Under the direction of Jimmy McPartland. Big deal you know, he was the booking agent. So as I said, we worked in Des Moines, Iowa there and...
That's a bit unusual isn't it? For a booking agent to put his name ....

Well he was smart. He put his name up there so that anybody would call it his band. It's like Meyer Davis and his orchestra under the direction of Jimmy McPartland you know. Or under the direction of Miles Davis. (LAUGHTER).
Listen, for future generations though would you explain what A and R is?

Artist and Repertoire. A and R man. So that's what Dick Voynow did. So we went out to Des Moines, Iowa. Now you can find that in your jazz history books a picture there of the band out in Des Moines, Iowa. Ten Cents a Dance it was, the place you know, an amusement park.

We came back to Chicago after that and he booked us another job, this Husk O'Hare did out in the White City Ballroom out on the South Side. And I'm proud to say that that band now was really swinging.
